The ""buffer_percent"" logic that is used by the ring buffer splice code to
only wake up the tasks when there's no data after the buffer is filled to
the percentage of the ""buffer_percent"" file is dependent on three
variables that determine the amount of data that is in the ring buffer:
1) pages_read - incremented whenever a new sub-buffer is consumed
2) pages_lost - incremented every time a writer overwrites a sub-buffer
3) pages_touched - incremented when a write goes to a new sub-buffer
The percentage is the calculation of:
(pages_touched - (pages_lost + pages_read)) / nr_pages
Basically
column2: the amount of data is the total number of sub-bufs that have been

column1: touched
column2: minus the number of sub-bufs lost and sub-bufs consumed. This is

column1: divided by the total count to give the buffer percentage. When the
percentage is greater than the value in the ""buffer_percent"" file
wakes up splice readers waiting for that amount.
It was observed that over time
column2: the amount read from the splice was

column1: constantly decreasing the longer the trace was running. That is
asked for 60%
column2: it would read over 60% when it first starts tracing

column1: then it would be woken up at under 60% and would slowly decrease the
amount of data read after being woken up
less than the buffer percent.
This was due to an accounting of the pages_touched incrementation. This
value is incremented whenever a writer transfers to a new sub-buffer. But
the place where it was incremented was incorrect. If a writer overflowed
the current sub-buffer it would go to the next one. If it gets preempted
by an interrupt at that time
column2: and the interrupt performs a trace

column1: will end up going to the next sub-buffer. But only one should increment
the counter. Unfortunately
Change the cmpxchg() that does the real switch of the tail-page into a
try_cmpxchg()
column3: perform the increment of pages_touched. This

column1: will only increment the counter once for when the writer moves to a new
sub-buffer
column2: and not when there's a race and is incremented for when a

column1: writer and its preempting writer both move to the same new sub-buffer.
